previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), type 2 diabetes, COPD, schizophrenia, and cocaine use was admitted for acute decompensation of systolic heart failure following recent crack use. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and productive cough. Initial treatment with IV furosemide showed limited response, prompting transfer to cardiology and a trial of IV lasix drip, which led to significant fluid loss and symptom improvement. Due to poor oral absorption, he was transitioned to torsemide 60 mg daily. His diabetes was complicated by hypoglycemia, requiring reduction and subsequent adjustment of insulin glargine. Cocaine use was directly linked to the decompensation, and he was referred to an addiction program and psychiatry for ongoing support. He stabilized, lost weight, and was discharged home with close follow-up, strict instructions to avoid cocaine and sodium, and a plan to monitor daily weights.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Shortness of breath, decreased Lasix.

COMPARISON:  Chest CTA ___ and chest radiograph ___.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Moderate enlargement of the cardiac
silhouette is unchanged.  The mediastinal contours are stable, with widening
of the right paratracheal stripe compatible with underlying mediastinal
lymphadenopathy.  Diffuse interstitial markings are again seen with
ground-glass opacities, perhaps minimally worse in the right lung base
compared to the prior study.  These findings are compatible with chronic
interstitial lung disease with a possible superimposed process.  No pleural
effusion or pneumothorax is identified.  There are no acute osseous
abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:  Diffuse lung disease, with slight interval worsening of
opacification in the right lung base.  These findings may reflect superimposed
pulmonary edema on a background of chronic lung disease, though these findings
could also be related to acute exacerbation of a recurrent pulmonary
abnormality.
